title: Hawthorne Studies Explained Simply | Principles of Management Ep 11
description:
Ravi pays his Chai Corner team well, but the team is quiet and the chai is slow. More money changes nothing. Then he sits down and simply listens, and the next morning everyone works faster. In this animated lesson we use his chai stall to understand the human relations approach to management.

You will learn how Elton Mayo and Fritz Roethlisberger of Harvard explained the Hawthorne studies at Western Electric's Hawthorne Works near Chicago (1924-1932), stage by stage: the lighting tests, the relay assembly test room, the interview programme with over 20,000 workers, and the bank wiring room. Then we sum up what Mayo learned: workers are social beings, attention raises output (the Hawthorne effect), informal groups shape how hard people work, and money is not the only motivator.

This is Episode 11 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
